concepts.title: Three Continents in One Life
concepts.definition: Jhumpa Lahiri's narrator compresses a migrant life into one arc: India, where he was born and his mother died; England, where he lived in a house with other Bengali bachelors near the London School of Economics; and America -- the third and final continent -- where he arrives to a job at a university library and a pre-arranged marriage.
concepts.key_idea: One life, three continents -- migration measured not in miles but in everything left behind.
concepts.textbook_ref: keww106.txt journey sections (india birth and mother's death, london years near lse, arrival in america, arranged marriage to mala)
question_patterns: which three continents does the narrator live on
in class 11 the third and final continent: why does the narrator leave for america

how does the narrator remember his mother across the journey

solution_steps.explain: The narrator carries his mother's death in Calcutta and years of bachelor drudgery in London.
A library job in Boston and a marriage arranged through family bring him to the final continent.
Lahiri folds decades of migration into quiet details -- a Grundig reel-to-reel, fried eggs, guidebooks.

concepts.title: Mrs Croft of Malden: 103 and Free of Illusion
concepts.definition: The narrator lodges with Mrs Croft, a hundred-and-three-year-old widow in Malden who insists on proper dress, walks with the help of her daughter, and was born the decade slavery's shadows still touched memory. Her fierce routines -- stamping her cane, demanding he declare 'a great adventure' -- teach the immigrant discipline and warmth at once.
concepts.key_idea: A hundred-year-old landlady outlives centuries and teaches the newcomer how to stand tall in a new world.
concepts.textbook_ref: keww106.txt mrs croft sections (mrs croft age 103, malden house, declaring a great adventure, proper attire, helen her daughter)
question_patterns: describe mrs croft and her habits in the story
in class 11 the third and final continent: why does mrs croft insist the narrator dress properly

solution_steps.explain: Mrs Croft is over a century old, upright, exacting and secretly kind -- a relic with rules.
She inspects his dress, listens for her daughter, and demands he declare his lodgings 'a great adventure' before she is satisfied.
Her fierce dignity steadies the newcomer's first days in the new world.

concepts.title: Mala, the Marriage That Becomes Home
concepts.definition: Mala arrives, a stranger in a saree, and the marriage begins in shyness. Sharing the news of Mrs Croft's death, the couple find their first true bond; years later, driving with their American-born son, the narrator counts their decades of marriage as the ordinary miracle of an immigrant life quietly made whole.
concepts.key_idea: Strangers become spouses become home -- love arriving slowly, the immigrant's quietest achievement.
concepts.textbook_ref: keww106.txt mala sections (mala's arrival in boston, shared grief over mrs croft, growing bond, son born in america, decades of marriage)
question_patterns: how does the relationship between the narrator and mala develop

solution_steps.explain: The arranged couple start with silence and unfamiliarity -- two exiles sharing a flat.
News of Mrs Croft's death at over a hundred creates their first tears shared together.
By the end the narrator sees their long marriage, his son, and their settled life as his greatest adventure.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Why does Mrs Croft make the narrator declare that America is 'a great adventure'?

solution_template.explain: She stands by the door and demands he pronounce the words before she is satisfied.
It is her way of insisting the newcomer greet the new world with wonder, not weariness.
The absurd little ceremony plants the story's seed -- that migration can be adventure, not only loss.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Mrs Croft's death brings the narrator and his wife closer. Explain how.

solution_template.explain: The narrator comes home to tell Mala that the old landlady has died at last.
For the first time they weep together for someone neither can replace -- grief as first intimacy.
From that night the marriage turns from arrangement to companionship -- the quiet turning point of the story.
